facts.fact_text: According to the applicant, the demonstrations of 31 July 2010 and 10 March 2013 were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations of 31 July 2010 and 10 March 2013 were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 31 July 2010.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 10 March 2013.
Shortly after the demonstration of 31 July 2010 had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
Shortly after the demonstration of 10 March 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation at the demonstration of 31 July 2010.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation at the demonstration of 10 March 2013.
On 23 July 2010 the organisers, consisting of several members of opposition parties, gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) of the demonstration planned for 31 July 2010.
It appears that no prior notice was given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) by the organisers of the demonstration of 10 March 2013.

At the time of the applicant's arrests on 31 July 2010 and 10 March 2013, under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 (CAO) provided that any breach of the rules, set forth under the legislation, on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen manats (AZN).

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 (CAO) provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with a lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five manats (AZN) or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by up to fifteen days' administrative detention.

By a decision of 31 July 2010, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
By a decision of 31 July 2010, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) sentenced the applicant to seven days' administrative detention.
By a decision of 11 March 2013, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
By a decision of 11 March 2013, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) sentenced the applicant to seven days' administrative detention.

According to the applicant, he was never served with copies of the administrative offence reports from his case files in either the first case (31 July 2010) or the second case (10 March 2013).
According to the applicant, he was never served with other material from his case files in either the first case (31 July 2010) or the second case (10 March 2013).
In the first case (arrest on 31 July 2010), the applicant was not given access to a lawyer after the arrest or while he was in police custody.
In the second case (arrest on 10 March 2013), the applicant was not given access to a lawyer after the arrest or while he was in police custody.
According to the applicant, in the first case (31 July 2010), the applicant was not given an opportunity to appoint a lawyer of his own choosing at the court hearing before the Sabail District Court.

According to the applicant, in the second case (11 March 2013), the applicant was not given an opportunity to appoint a lawyer of his own choosing at the court hearing before the Sabail District Court.
At the Sabail District Court hearing in the first case (31 July 2010), the applicant was not represented by a lawyer.
According to the material submitted to the Court by the parties in the first case, the applicant refused legal assistance at the Sabail District Court hearing on 31 July 2010.
It appears that at the Sabail District Court hearing in the second case (11 March 2013), a State-funded lawyer was invited to represent the applicant.

None of the material submitted to the Court contains any records showing that the State-funded lawyer, Ms E.Z., made any oral submissions to the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) in the second case (11 March 2013).

None of the material submitted to the Court contains any records showing that the State-funded lawyer, Ms E.Z., made any written submissions to the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) in the second case (11 March 2013).
